steps.title: Import Vue and defineProps
steps.instruction: Import Vue and defineProps from 'vue' to set up prop validation.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Vue and defineProps from the 'vue' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing from a package
import { ref, computed } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue and defineProps functions are imported and ready for use.
successCriteria: Vue and defineProps are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported Vue and defineProps, which are essential for creating components with prop validation.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both Vue and defineProps from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to import both Vue and defineProps from the 'vue' package.

steps.title: Create the main Vue component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named 'PropTypeDemo' with a script section and a template section. The template should return a div element.
steps.hint: In Vue single-file components, you define the component with <script> and <template> tags. The template should contain the HTML structure.
steps.analogousExample: // Example Vue component structure
steps.seedCode:
<script>
// Import Vue and defineProps here
</script>

<template>
  <!-- Add a div element here -->
</template>
steps.expectedOutcome: A Vue component named 'PropTypeDemo' with script and template sections is created.
successCriteria: The component is named 'PropTypeDemo' and contains both <script> and <template> sections with a div in the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the main Vue component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the component is named 'PropTypeDemo' and has both script and template sections with a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure isn't quite right. Remember to create a Vue component with script and template sections, and name it 'PropTypeDemo'.

steps.title: Define prop types for a user object
steps.instruction: Inside the defineProps function, define a prop object with three properties: name (string), age (number), and isActive (boolean).
steps.hint: Use defineProps with an object where each property specifies its type using the appropriate constructor (String, Number, Boolean).
steps.seedCode:
<script>
// Import Vue and defineProps here
</script>

<template>
  <!-- Add a div element here -->
</template>

<script setup>
defineProps({
  // Define name, age, and isActive props here
})
</script>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have properly typed props for a user object with name, age, and isActive properties.
successCriteria: defineProps is called with an object containing name: String, age: Number, and isActive: Boolean properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the prop types for the user object.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have all three properties with the correct types.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're using defineProps with an object containing name: String, age: Number, and isActive: Boolean.

steps.title: Add required and default values for props
steps.instruction: In the defineProps configuration, mark the 'name' prop as required and set default values for 'age' (default to 25) and 'isActive' (default to false).
steps.hint: Use the 'required' property for name and 'default' property for age and isActive in the prop definitions.
steps.seedCode:
<script>
// Import Vue and defineProps here
</script>

<template>
  <!-- Add a div element here -->
</template>

<script setup>
defineProps({
  // Define name, age, and isActive props here
  name: {
    type: String,
    required: true
  },
  age: {
    type: Number,
    default: 25
  },
  isActive: {
    type: Boolean,
    default: false
  }
})
</script>
steps.expectedOutcome: The name prop will be required, while age and isActive will have default values when not provided.
successCriteria: The defineProps configuration includes required: true for name and default values for age (25) and isActive (false).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've correctly configured the prop requirements and defaults.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added both the required property for name and default values for age and isActive.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've properly configured the prop definitions with required and default properties.

steps.title: Create template to display user data
steps.instruction: Inside the template section, add a <div> element that displays the user's name, age, and active status using the props defined in defineProps.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to output prop values in the template. For example, {{ name }} will display the name prop value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will show the user's name, age, and whether they are active when the component receives props.
successCriteria: The template contains a <div> with three elements that display the name, age, and isActive prop values using {{ }} syntax.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully displayed the prop data in the template. The user information will now be visible when props are passed to the component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're displaying all three prop values (name, age, and isActive) inside the template using the correct syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet display the prop data correctly. Remember to use double curly braces {{ }} to output the prop values inside the template.

steps.title: Add component state for local data
steps.instruction: Add a reactive state variable called 'message' using Vue's ref function, initialized with the string 'Hello from local state!'.
steps.hint: Use the ref function from Vue to create reactive state. Import it if needed, then declare it inside your component.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a reactive 'message' state variable alongside the props, ready to be used in the template.
successCriteria: A reactive state variable named 'message' is declared using ref, initialized with the string 'Hello from local state!'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added reactive state to your component using Vue's ref.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've declared 'message' using ref with the correct initial value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The reactive state variable 'message' is not correctly defined. Check that you're using ref from Vue with the proper initialization.

steps.title: Create method to update local state
steps.instruction: Create a method named 'updateMessage' that updates the local message state when called.
steps.hint: Define a function inside the script setup that changes the value of the message ref.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a method that can modify the message state when invoked.
successCriteria: A function named 'updateMessage' is defined that updates the 'message' ref value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the updateMessage method that modifies the local state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you define a function named 'updateMessage' that changes the 'message' ref value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The method wasn't created correctly. Define a function called 'updateMessage' that updates the message state.

steps.title: Add button to trigger method
steps.instruction: In the template section, add a button element that calls the updateMessage method when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the @click directive to bind the click event to your method.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Example: button triggering a method -->
<button @click="handleClick">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Update Message' appears in the UI, which when clicked will trigger the updateMessage method.
successCriteria: Button element with @click directive calling updateMessage is added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a button that triggers the updateMessage method when clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it uses @click="updateMessage" to call the method.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button isn't properly wired to the updateMessage method. Check that you're using @click with the correct method name.

steps.title: Add computed property based on props
steps.instruction: Add a computed property named 'userInfo' that returns a formatted string combining the name, age, and isActive props.
steps.hint: Use the computed function from Vue to create a reactive property that depends on props. Access props directly in the computed function.
steps.expectedOutcome: A computed property 'userInfo' is defined that formats the user props into a descriptive string.
successCriteria: The computed property 'userInfo' is defined using computed() and returns a string combining name, age, and isActive status.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a computed property that formats user information based on props.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using computed() and accessing the props correctly to create the formatted string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The computed property isn't defined correctly. Check that you're using computed() and returning a string with the user data.

steps.title: Display computed property in template
steps.instruction: In the template, add a paragraph element that displays the computed userInfo property.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to output the computed property value in the template.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a computed property in template

{{ fullName }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will show the computed user information when the component renders.
successCriteria: A paragraph element exists in the template that displays the userInfo computed property value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully displayed the computed property in the template, completing the component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the correct syntax {{ userInfo }} to display the computed property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The computed property isn't displayed in the template. Add a paragraph element with {{ userInfo }}.
